To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) β3AR and/or β1AR expression is decreased in adipose tissue in all models of obesity tested, 2) the degree of obesity is inversely related to adipocyte βAR subtype expression, 3) the degree of β3AR expression in BAT is less affected by obesity than that in WAT, and 4) β2AR expression is increased in BAT in the obese Lepoband Lep Rdb mice
The expression of βARs is decreased in all models of obesity in mice, and that the extent of decrease correlates with the degree of obesity.
obesity is associated with impaired expression of adipocyte beta-adrenergic (AR) subtypes, and that the degree of impaired AR expression correlates with the severity of obesity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how adipocytes respond to signals that promote the storage or release of fat.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of human obesity and the metabolic disorders associated with it.
the regulation of the β-adrenergically mediated lipolytic pathway in white and brown fat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
obesity is associated with a decrease in the expression of βAR subtypes, particularly β3AR.
obesity is associated with decreased βAR expression in adipose tissue.
βAR expression is reduced in adipose tissue in all models of obesity studied to date.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of the β3-AR is down-regulated in obesity.
the obese state is associated with a decrease in βAR expression and function in WAT, and that the degree of obesity is related to the magnitude of the decrease.
obesity-related changes in the expression of adipose tissue AR subtypes are a general feature in rodents, and are correlated with the degree of obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adipose βAR expression is impaired in obesity.
the obese phenotype of mice and men is not caused by a lack of β3ARs in adipose tissue, as originally proposed.
obesity is associated with impaired βAR expression in adipose tissue.
